o1.biggest_strength: It finds the real levers in the data, ranks them well, and gives believable ranges with the working shown.
o1.biggest_mistake: The day-3 message only goes to scanned parcels, so it may miss some of the silence that is creating WISMO tickets; I would tighten that trigger.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add a clearer day-3 no-scan customer message/escalation, remove the dated Christmas/November assumptions unless confirmed, and include one more bra-specific post-delivery fit nudge.

o2.biggest_strength: Very practical and complete: it covers the messages, portal, fit quiz placement, rollout order, holdout, and numbers cleanly.
o2.biggest_mistake: It adds an assumed 2-hour size-change window and a few extra touches without proving they are feasible, and some copy is a little less on-brand than Output 1.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make the operational assumptions lighter, sharpen the brand language around bra fit, and rank the expected value of the three fixes more explicitly.

reason: Both are usable, but Output 1 is the one I would act on first because it is more commercially decisive and more careful about not over-claiming the fit finder gain. Output 2 has a fuller flow, but it leans on an unproven size-change operation and feels a little less like our voice.
